It is but fifteen years since the first line . . . was constructed in this country and at the present time there are not less than 50,000 miles in successful operation on this continent, having over 1,400 stations, and employing upwards of 10,000 operators and clerks. The number of messages passing over all the lines in this country annually is estimated at upwards of 5,000,000, producing a revenue of $2,000,000. . . .

—Atlantic Monthly, March 1860

The invention discussed in this article led directly to —

options.label: F
options.text: the expansion of educational opportunities for women

options.label: G
options.text: rapid communication of information to distant locations

options.label: H
options.text: the increased ability of people to work at night

options.label: J
options.text: rapid population growth in the western territories
